title: Collections and iterators mind map
intro: C# programs spend most of their time moving data between collections. This module covers arrays, the four generic workhorses (List, Dictionary, HashSet, Queue), IEnumerable/foreach, yield-based deferred sequences, C# 12 collection expressions, frozen and immutable read-only snapshots, and when to reach for a BCL type instead of inventing your own.

conceptCards.title: Arrays (fixed-length)
conceptCards.summary: Fixed Length, O(1) indexing, reference type on the heap. Span<T> is a zero-copy view — full rules in module 17.

conceptCards.title: List, Dictionary, HashSet, Queue
conceptCards.summary: The four generic types in System.Collections.Generic. Append, lookup, membership, FIFO — each answers one question. Dictionary resizes and needs IEqualityComparer.

conceptCards.title: IEnumerable and foreach
conceptCards.summary: foreach is GetEnumerator, MoveNext, Current, and Dispose. IEnumerable<T> is walkable, not necessarily materialized.

conceptCards.title: Iterators and yield
conceptCards.summary: yield return builds a state machine. Execution is deferred until enumeration. Two foreach calls re-run the work.
conceptCards.example: IEnumerable<string[]> rows = ReadCsvRows(path); // file not read yet

conceptCards.title: Collection expressions
conceptCards.summary: C# 12 bracket syntax [1, 2, ..rest]. Always eager — not LINQ, not lazy.

conceptCards.title: Use the BCL first
conceptCards.summary: Channel<T> for async pipes (module 15). FrozenDictionary for startup config. Do not invent a custom queue.

conceptCards.title: Frozen and immutable collections
conceptCards.summary: Read-only snapshots for startup config and shared lookups. FrozenDictionary for max speed; ImmutableDictionary for versioned updates.
